en: A catalog of thirty fascicles, including the original manuscripts of the Great Abbot Kōben and others;
twenty-nine fascicles have purple-dyed silk covers, twenty-five fascicles have outer titles, five fascicles lack outer titles, and one fascicle lacks a cover.

The newly translated *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* consists of one work in four fascicles, each fascicle comprising ten volumes; however, at the end of the fourth fascicle, there is a preface by the King of South India regarding the presentation of the Sanskrit manuscript. These four fascicles are the first, second, third, and fourth.

*Commentary on the Benevolent King Prajñāpāramitā Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *The Chapter on the Lotus Great Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas from the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva within the Ritual Teachings of the Vajraśekhara Trailokyavijaya*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *Ritual for the Recitation of the Yoga Lotus Family*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *Ritual for the Recitation of the One-Syllable Cūḍāmaṇi King*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *Sarvayogayogin Sūtra of the Vajraśikhara Kūṭāgāra*, one fascicle; translated by Vajrabodhi. *Yoga of the One-Syllable Cūḍāmaṇi King*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. [Postscript: *Ultimate Ritual Manual for the Yoga of the One-Syllable Cūḍāmaṇi King*, one fascicle. The above constitutes one volume, the fifth bundle.

The Newly Translated Benevolent Kings Sūtra, two fascicles; translated by Amoghavajra. The One-Syllable Extraordinary Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Sūtra, three fascicles; translated by Amoghavajra. The Avalokiteśvara Vidyārāja Sūtra, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. The Prophecy of Avalokiteśvara Sūtra, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. The Subsequent title reads: The Ritual Manual of the Bodhisattva Tārā Avalokiteśvara. The Uṣṇīṣavijayā Ritual Manual, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. The Akṣobhya Recitation Method, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. The Ekajaṭā Dhāraṇī Sūtra, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. The above constitutes one volume in the sixth bundle.
The *Ṣaṭpāramitā-sūtra*, one fascicle, ten volumes; this one work, one bundle, constitutes the seventh case.
The *Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā-sūtra*, one fascicle, ten volumes; this one work, one bundle, constitutes the eighth case.

*The Bodhimaṇḍa Ekākṣara-uṣṇīṣarāja Sūtra*, one fascicle in five rolls, translated by Amoghavajra; it begins with the *Sparśana-vidhi* (Sprinkling Purification) and includes the mantras of the various deities of the Garbhadhātu, the mantras of the Bodhisattvas for homa, and the Vajra Songs of Praise. *The Mahādevī Pramoda Sūtra*, one roll, translated by Amoghavajra; it concludes with the sequence of the eighteen neck-mantras (*kaṇṭha-mantra*). [This constitutes] the first item in the ninth fascicle.
*Vajraśekhara-saṃkṣipta-niryūha-sūtra*, one work in four fascicles; this one work, one scroll, constitutes the tenth bundle.
*Vajraśekhara-tattva-mahātantrarāja-sūtra*, one work in three fascicles, translated by Amoghavajra; this one work, one scroll, constitutes the eleventh bundle.
One volume of the newly translated *Ghanavyūha-sūtra*, in three fascicles, translated by Amoghavajra; this one work, comprising one fascicle, constitutes the twelfth bundle.
One volume of the *Ekādaśamukha-vidhi-sūtra*, in three fascicles; this one work, comprising one fascicle, constitutes the thirteenth bundle.

The *Amoghapāśa Sūtra*, two fascicles; the sixth [fascicle], at the end of the twentieth [section], contains a catalog of various sūtras, ritual manuals (*vidhi*), and so forth. The above two fascicles comprise one bundle (one *tie*) in the fourteenth case.

*Varṣābharaṇa-ratna-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, Chapter on the Alphabet, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra; *Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-japa-vidhi*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra; *Kṣipra-pratyaya-maheśvara-deva-bhāṣita-garuḍa-āvīśa-vidhi*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra; *Kṣitigarbha-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-dharmakāya-stotra*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra; *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-sūtra*, one fascicle (lower volume); *Tattvārtha-nāma-tantra-pañjikā*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra; *Aksamālā-viśeṣa-gāthā*, one fascicle. The above constitutes the fifteenth bundle.

*The Sūtra of Mālikadevī and the Flower Garland*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Parṇaśavarī Avalokiteśvara*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *The Sūtra of Hārītī*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *The Sūtra of the Universal Good Dhāraṇī Spoken by Avalokiteśvara*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *The Sūtra of the Correct Treatise on the King’s Dharma*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Yoga of Samantabhadra-Vajrasattva*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *The Vajraśekhara Sūtra: The Chapter on the Dharma of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva in the Yoga*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. The above constitutes the sixteenth case, Volume 16.

*The Sūtra on the Merit of Constructing Stūpas and Extending Life*, one fascicle; translated by Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā. *The Vajraśekhara Yoga Rosary Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. The colophon states: "Briefly extracted from among the hundred thousand verses of the extensive [text], etc.
*The Liturgical Text for Repentance and Paying Homage to the Names of the Thirty-five Buddhas*; the colophon states: "Extracted from the *Upāliparipṛcchā-sūtra*, etc."

*The Sūtra of the Wood-Bead Rosary*, translated by Amoghavajra, one fascicle; *The Method for the Cultivation of the Practice of Avalokiteśvararāja* from the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra, one fascicle; at the end [is] *The Essential Method for Recitation of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa of the Cakravartin King*, with the *Mantra for Offering Residual Food to Acala* and the *News of the Bodhisattvas*, one fascicle; the note states it applies to all Buddhas of the Uṣṇīṣa, translated by Amoghavajra; *The Method for Following the Seven-Limb Recitation* from the *Mahāvairocana-abhisaṃbodhi-vikurvaṇādhiṣṭhāna Sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa*, translated by Amoghavajra, one fascicle. The above constitutes the seventeenth bundle, one set.

One fascicle of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-rāja-yoga-dhyāna-jñāna-vidhi*, translated by Amoghavajra; one fascicle of the *Bodhimaṇḍala-vyūha-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra; and one fascicle of the *Ratnakaraṇḍa-sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra. The above constitutes the eighteenth bundle.

*The Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Great Yakṣiṇī Hārītī and Her Beloved Son* (with a note stating it is also called *The Ritual of Hārītī*; translated by Amoghavajra). *The Ritual Manual for the Recitation and Practice of Samantabhadra from the Tattvapatala of the Gaganagañja-parivarta of the Vajraśekhara-yoga* (translated by Amoghavajra). *The Ritual for the Recitation of the Vajrāyuṣa-dhāraṇī* (translated by Vajrabodhi and Amoghavajra). *The Mahā-pratītyasamutpāda-vairocana-buddha-mahābhiṣeka-prabhāsa-mantra*, one fascicle (with a note stating it is extracted from the twenty-eight fascicles of the *Amoghapāśa-sūtra*; contains Sanskrit characters; translated by Amoghavajra). *Treatise on the Arousing of Bodhicitta*, one fascicle (translated by Amoghavajra). *The Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Practice of Mahāsukha-vajrasattva*, one fascicle (with a note stating it is extracted from the *Śrī-paramādya-tantrarāja-yoga*; translated by Amoghavajra). The above constitutes one volume, the nineteenth bundle.

*Vajraśekhara-yoga-sūtra: Index to the Eighteen Assemblies*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *Homage and Repentance Rite for the Thirty-seven Honored Ones*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *Explanation of the Seventeen Honored Ones*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra. *Essential Outline of the Various Sections of the Dhāraṇī-gate*, one fascicle. *Commentary on the Homage to the Dharma-body of the Great Holy Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva*, which states: "This homage is extracted from the *Mahāyāna-sarvabuddhaviṣayajñānālokalaṃkāra-sūtra*; translated by Amoghavajra. *Ritual for Generating the Bodhicitta*, one fascicle. *Text for Bestowing the Precepts of Generating the Bodhicitta*, one fascicle. *Dharmakāya Mudrās and Seals of the One Hundred and Eight Honored Ones*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra and Wuxing. At the end is the *Dhāraṇī of the Corresponding Phrases Flowing Forth from the Vairocana Siddhi*. The above constitutes one fascicle, the twentieth bundle.

*The Ritual for the Recitation of the Benevolent Kings Sūtra*, one fascicle; within this, there are sections that expand upon the standard rules. *The Ritual Manual for the Five Secrets of Vajrasattva Yoga of the Vajraśekhara*, one fascicle. *The Secret Method of the Messenger of Acala*, one fascicle; the title note states: "Also known as the Mantra of the Difficult-to-Conquer Wrathful King. *The Method for Cultivating the Samādhi of Vairocana according to the Yoga of the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, translated by Vajrabodhi. The above constitutes one volume, the twenty-first case.

One fascicle of the *Mañjuśrī-mūla-kalparāja-vidyārāja-garuḍarāja-parivarta*; one fascicle of the *Mahāvaiśravaṇa-deva-harāja-dhāraṇī-vidhi*, translated by Prajñākara; and one fascicle of the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī*. The colophon at the end states: "Transmitted by the Venerable Mahāyāna of Gaogong Temple in Yuan County. This constitutes the twenty-second bundle, the first item in this set.

*Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle. At the beginning of this booklet, there are six lines of Sanskrit mantras, including 􄗦 (Oṃ), 􄙖 (Vajra), 􄕯 (Hūṃ), and 􅚤 (Svāhā); these may be verified by subsequent examination. Furthermore, at the beginning of the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā-mantra*, there is one line of prose stating, "At that time, the World-Honored One knew the thoughts and intentions in the mind of Śakra," which differs slightly from the standard versions of the text. *The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Greatly Majestic Wrathful King Acala, the Holy Immovable One, with the Supreme Standing Mudrā, from the Vajrapāṇi-prabhābhiṣeka-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Amoghavajra. The above constitutes one volume, the twenty-third bundle.
*Vajraśekhara-sūtra Mahāyoga-guhyacittabhūmi-dharmaparyāya-artha-ṭīkā*, Scroll One (upper). [This is] the twenty-fourth fascicle, the first item in the right-hand section.
*Āryakrodhavajrakumārabodhisiddhi-kalpa-sūtra* and *Mahāyānapratītyasamutpāda-śāstra*, one scroll each.
Composed by the Noble Ullangha; translated by Amoghavajra. Marked with vermilion headings. *Gadagana*.
One fascicle of the *Kongō* (Vajra) Mantra for bestowing food and drink upon all hungry ghosts; one scroll of the *Mañjuśrī-bodhisattva-utsarjana-buddhāṭana-dhāraṇī*;
next, the Sanskrit-syllable mantra of Hārītī; next, the Sanskrit-syllable mantra of the Beloved Son (*Priyaputra*) along with its ritual instructions;
next, the Sanskrit-syllable mantra for bestowing food upon the Four Heavenly Kings along with its ritual instructions.
Next, the *Acala-bhaṭṭāraka-saṃskṛta-mantra* with its commentary; next, the *Sanskrit-Chinese Commentary on the Eight Maṇḍala Sūtras*;

next, the *Mañjuśrī-mūla-kalparāja-vidyādhara-pakṣirāja-parivarta*, one fascicle—this appears to be a duplicate of a previous edition found within the twenty-second bundle; next, the *Ārya-yamāntaka-krūra-rāja-sthiti*.

*The Ritual for Recitation of Great Efficacy*, one fascicle. It contains Sanskrit characters, followed by the *Bodhisattva’s Verse on the Summer Retreat* (*Varṣā*) and the *Verse on the Prātimokṣa* (*Pravāraṇā*).
However, this *Pravāraṇā* verse differs from the standard versions; is it perhaps the *Bodhi-Pravāraṇā* verse?
The root mantra of Mahātejas Krodharāja has its phrases demarcated with ink; subsequently, there is a record of various similar and different versions of the world-system.
The preceding verses follow the sequence of the text; this is the "Preface to the Dedication" (Huixiang Wen) lectured upon by Master Huayan.
May these sounds transform all things, and so forth. This single fascicle contains no external title nor a name for the binding case.
One fascicle of the *Āryakāṇicandaroṣaṇavajrakumārabodhisiddhividhi-sūtra*; one fascicle of the *Vajrakumārajāpavidhi-sūtra*. These two works in one volume have no outer title nor a case name.
*The Meaning of the Contemplation Gate of Cintāmaṇicakra Bodhisattva with Secret Instructions*, one fascicle;
*The Yoga of the Vajraśekhara Sūtra: Commentary on the Chapter on the Alphabet*, one fascicle (with Sanskrit characters);

*The Contemplation Gate of the Forty-two Letters from the "Entering the Dharma Realm" Chapter of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, one fascicle (with Sanskrit characters); *The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya*.
*The Ritual Manual for the Yoga of the Syllable-Wheel of Vairocana’s Dharmakāya from the “Entrance into the Dharma Realm” Chapter*, one fascicle;

*The Essential Catalogue of Various Sections of Dhāraṇīs*, one fascicle (which contains three minor mantras in Sanskrit characters; my private note says they are the same as those previously mentioned);
*The Text for Bestowing the Bodhisattva Precepts*, one fascicle (which contains Sanskrit characters; my private note says it is the same as the previous one).

*Commentary on the Meaning of the Great Maṇḍala of the Seventeen Holy Ones of the Bodhisattva Amoghasiddhi-vajra of Great Bliss, according to the *Prajñāpāramitā-naya-sūtra*, one scroll. [Private note: I say this is likely the same as the previous version.
*The Index to the Eighteen Assemblies of the Vajraśekhara-yoga Sūtra*, one scroll. Translated by Amoghavajra. [Private note: I say it is the same as the previous [work].

Is it the same? *The Ritual Text for the Homage and Repentance of the Vairocana Tathāgata’s Own Body as the Inner-Realized Wisdom Retinue within the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu according to the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, the Supreme Vehicle Secret Samādhi of the Buddhas, one fascicle;
translated by Amoghavajra. [Private note: Is this the same as the previous one? However, the end is incomplete. (1) Right.
The fascicles have no outer titles nor titles on their covers;
however, there is a table of contents for each fascicle on the inner side of the cover.

*The Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, Chapter on the Alphabet, Volume 14; *The Vajraśekhara-sūtra Commentary on the Yoga of the Sanskrit Alphabet*, one fascicle; *The Mahāvaipulya-buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra, Gaṇḍavyūha-parivarta: The Contemplation Gate of the Forty-two Letters*, with Sanskrit characters (I privately note: is this the same text as the preceding one?). *The Mahāvaipulya-buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra, Gaṇḍavyūha-parivarta: The Contemplation Gate of the Forty-two Letters*, one fascicle (I privately note: is this the same text as the preceding one? It differs only in that it contains the Sanskrit *akṣara-cakra*). *The Dharani-akṣara-vyavahāra-pratipatti-paṭala*, one fascicle; *The Renwang Banruo Boluomiduo Shi: The Mantra Method for Turning the Wheel of Dharma by Bodhisattva Cūḍāmaṇi to Subdue Demons and Enemies*, one fascicle. The above is one bundle; it lacks an outer title and a box name.

One copy of the *Sanskrit* *Ārya-Sahasranetra-Sahasramukha-Sahasrajihvā-Sahasrabhuja-Avalokiteśvara-Bodhisattva-Mahāvistara-Pūrṇa-Asaṅga-Mahākaruṇācitta-Dhāraṇī*; one copy of the *Sanskrit* *Mahāvajracakra-Mantra*; one copy of the *Sanskrit* *Acala-Karuṇāmocana-Vidyā*; the *Sanskrit* *Aṣṭadaśamārga-Mantras* and others; the *Sanskrit* *Gaganagañja-Vyūha-Vidyā*; the *Sanskrit* *Cintāmaṇicakra-Stotra*; the *Sanskrit* *Cintāmaṇicakra-Mantra*; the *Sanskrit* *Amṛtakuṇḍalī-Mantra*; the *Sanskrit* *Ṣaḍpāda-Bhagavat-Kāya-Mantra*; the *Sanskrit* *Vajrapramardana-Mantra*; the *Sanskrit* *Lokadhara-Mantra*. Next, there are the *Sanskrit* *Mahāmantras*: ॐ वाक्युरत्नधराणि (Oṃ Vākya-ratnadhārāṇi), etc., etc. If it is the *Prasannapadā* (or *Sādhanamālā*), it may be known by examining it.

The Sanskrit syllable mantra for the five-pronged [vajra]; the Sanskrit syllable mantra for the bell; the Sanskrit syllable mantra for the three-pronged [vajra]; the Sanskrit syllable mantra for the single-pronged [vajra]; the Sanskrit syllable mantra for the *karma* of the Vajra Family; the Sanskrit syllable mantra for the *karma* of the Ratna Family; the Sanskrit syllable mantra for the *karma* of the Padma Family; the Sanskrit syllable mantra for the *karma* of the Karma Family; and the Sanskrit syllable mantra for the small vajra-wheel. Following these, there are further Sanskrit syllable mantras, such as 􄖩􄗭􄖩􄖩􄙖􄧀􈂳 and so forth, which may be verified through consultation.

The Sanskrit-syllable Bodhisattva-alaṃkāra-mantra, the Sahacitta-mantra, and the Sahacittānuvartana-mantra; below these are the meanings of their functional powers. Next are the Sanskrit-syllable Vajra-vimukti-mantra and other Sanskrit-syllable mantras, which may be verified through comparison.

The Ritual Manual for the *Dhāraṇī of the Gateways to Boundless Emanation* Spoken by the Buddha, translated by Amoghavajra; the Sixteen Bodhisattva Samayas in Sanskrit from the *Tattvasaṃgraha Maṇḍala*; the Ritual Manual for the One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa in Sanskrit; the Chinese-language Auspicious Praises;
the Mantra for Severing the Bite of Snakes and Scorpions; the Mantra for Warding off Mosquitoes; and the Incense Burning and Flower Scattering Rites.

One fascicle of the *Method for the One-Syllable Root Dhāraṇī of Mañjuśrī* from the *Extensive Vaipulya Bodhisattva Piṭaka Sūtra*, including the verses on fragrant water and so forth. At the end it says: "On the twenty-third day of the first month of the third year of the Chang’an era, translated from the Sanskrit original by the Tripiṭaka Master Ānandajñāna of North India; the Brahmin Grand Chief Minister Li Wuchan served as the interpreter, and the monk Śrīmattra acted as the proofreader. There is one set of mantras for extinguishing the evil destinies, which I privately note as being slightly different from the usual versions. There is also one set of mantras for breaking through hell. On the outer title of this right-hand fascicle it says:
The Sanskrit-syllable mantras, etc.; however, many contain Chinese characters and the like. The above twenty-nine fascicles all have purple covers.
*Samantabhadra-Vajrasattva-Yoga-Paṭhavidhi* (One Fascicle), translated by Amoghavajra; this one fascicle has a damaged cover.
Furthermore, there may have originally been the ritual manual for Mañjuśrī at the beginning;
however, it has all been lost,
and only the final colophon remains.
On the twenty-seventh day of the second month in the eighteenth year of Enkyō,

the Left Dignitary (Saibenkan) submitted the following report from the Lower Tōji Temple regarding the matter of the thirty fascicles of dharma texts and registers obtained by Kūkai— posthumously honored as the Great Sōjō and the Fundamental Ajari of Shingon— who traveled to Tang China to seek them out, and their subsequent placement in the scripture repository: [End of Document]
The Right Grand Councillor has issued this imperial decree: "The aforementioned Dharma texts are to be fully collected within the Tripitaka and shall not be allowed to leave the country.
Order the Head of the Sect to protect them perpetually; the temple authorities must take cognizance of this proclamation and carry it out accordingly, without negligence."

The second day of the eleventh month in the nineteenth year of Enkyō. The Grand Historian, Kanna no Ashihiko Seihō, and the Great Debater, Tachibana no Ashihiko Seijō, requested that the imperial decree concerning the Great Monk be collected.
Of the thirty fascicles in total, twenty-nine have black-purple silk covers, while one lacks a cover.
Recorded on the sixth day of the sixth month in the eighteenth year of the Zhenguan era by the Acting Vinaya Master Zhiran.
The *Sūtra of the Peacock* and other texts, including the *Sūtra of the Son of the Strategy*, totaling eight types of ritual manuals (*vidhi*), were transcribed on paper.
Having completed the transcription and returned them, they were received as authentic.

On the second day of the eleventh month of the nineteenth year of Enryaku, these items—one bundle of draft manuscripts for the aforementioned sūtras, contained in a lined brown cloth bag with a brocade seam—were granted from the Imperial Palace.
Furthermore, there is one imperial edict from the Left Office of the Eastern Temple (Jimon) dated the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month of the second year of Tenmei.
Zenjō recorded that he completed the transcription on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month of the second year of Tenmei, using the original copy from Hōkōdai.
